limitations: Complete native span ends after the native call and final CUDA synchronization; process startup, report building and CLI output are excluded.

The five explicit input-directory manifests do not prove self-contained Triton dependencies or actual cache hits. Triton group metadata retains absolute references to the first empty-cache run. The formal Axolotl populated cohort additionally pins that original tree read-only and audits all referenced contents before and after every formal process. OS caches, dataset caches, clocks and system load remain inherited.

The original Axolotl populated calibration-1 finished before the source tree was made read-only, and calibration-2 was running at that time. Those calibrations and original holdouts-1/2 are diagnostic evidence, without retrospective claims of before/after dependency control. Four additional fixed processes provide two new calibrations and two new holdouts; original holdout-3 started after the new forecast seal and is reused as formal holdout-1 with explicit boundary audits.

Populated mode is unavailable when the first empty-cache run produced no artifacts. Read-only permission bits and boundary hashes are reproducibility evidence, not protection against an owner modifying permissions or ancestor directories, and do not establish control over all caches.

Formal forecasts were sealed before their holdout execution. Original diagnostic forecasts and comparisons are retained separately, including the original comparison for the reused physical process. Cost coverage is empirical and does not guarantee accuracy for another model, dataset, software stack, GPU, random sampler, packing or longer memory growth.
Allocated/reserved ranges are complete-run allocator observations, not confidence bounds, total device usage or additive per-window memory measurements.

OOM controls constrain the PyTorch per-process allocator fraction. They are real native training allocation failures and successful controls, not physical-card exhaustion or an exact minimum-VRAM determination.
Source checkpoint and framework installations were not modified. Path substitution changes bound identities, so this archive cannot be used as calibration input.

The first Hugging Face native calibration completed successfully, then an observation-validator allowlist rejected its framework during acceptance. Its raw report and failed matrix summary are preserved. Only the validator allowlist and one regression test changed between the original and final source freezes; collector and native matrix sources did not change. A separate continuation reused that calibration, ran one new calibration, then sealed predictions before three new holdouts.
